Adenocarcinoma arising in a uterine ligament, a reproductive structure outside the axes.
Developmental lung and pulmonary capillary disease defined by severe pulmonary hypertension and refractory hypoxemia.
Cerebellar degeneration with frequent peripheral neuropathy; nystagmus and diplopia reflect neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.
Ingrown beard hairs cause persistent perifollicular skin inflammation and sometimes scarring.
Inherited epidermal fragility with blistering and erosions; muscle, renal and hearing disease belong to uncommon subtypes.
Congenital absence of the lens with iris hypoplasia, microphthalmia and microcornea defines an ocular malformation syndrome.
Intermittent atrioventricular conduction failure defines a cardiac conduction disorder.
Combined immunodeficiency defines the umbrella; additional affected organs vary across its constituent syndromes.
Hereditary cerebral white-matter disease with megalencephaly; no common extra-neurologic organ damage is established.

Developmental abnormalities of the anterior segment of the eye define this spectrum.
Inherited lipid metabolism disorder; atherosclerotic disease and pancreatitis are separately diagnosed complications, not universal organ involvement.
Benign cutaneous neoplasm arising from eccrine sweat ducts.
Benign neoplasm located in the stomach.
Neck cancer lacks a specified tissue of origin; pulmonary assignment follows the sole supplied subtype, pharynx cancer, but may not cover the whole umbrella.

Developmental delay, characteristic blood changes and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; skin/nail abnormalities 30-99%; dental abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.

Benign smooth-muscle neoplasm arising in an extrahepatic bile duct; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Congenital absence of toes is a structural skeletal malformation.
Skeletal growth abnormalities, patellar defects and microtia define Meier-Gorlin syndrome; microtia occurs in 3/3; feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.
Immune-mediated non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation of lung parenchyma; no additional organ meets the threshold for this pulmonary concept.
Cardiac and skeletal developmental phenotype; coagulation abnormality 2/2 and developmental delay 2/5; keratosis pilaris 3/5 omitted by cap.
Mitochondrial myopathy with immunodeficiency 2/2 and low CD4 cells 3/4; hepatic injury supported by raised transaminases 3/4 and steatosis; neurologic findings omitted by cap.
